sections.html:
Provo is the Utah County seat, about 43 miles south of Salt Lake City on the eastern shore of Utah Lake. Of its 44.19 square miles, 41.69 are land and 2.50 are water, and the elevation is roughly 4,550 feet, with Orem to the north and Springville to the south. ZIP codes 84601 through 84606 apply.

Interstate 15 passes along the western side, US 89 (State Street) crosses the city from northwest to southeast, and US 189 ties State Street, I-15, BYU and Orem together. The whitewashed Y on the mountain is the landmark everyone knows.

Fort Utah, founded in 1849 by 33 Mormon families on land that had been home to the Timpanogos, grew into the city, which was incorporated in April 1850 and renamed for the trapper Etienne Provost, who reached the region in 1825. Provo Woolen Mills opened in 1872 as Utah's first large factory and ran until 1932, and Brigham Young Academy, the forerunner of BYU, was founded in 1875. Orchards earned the town the name Garden City.

The housing stock covers many decades, so condition varies a lot from street to street.

Provo leans toward rentals, with just 39.4% of housing units owner-occupied. The 2020 count was 115,162 residents, and the July 1, 2025 estimate is 114,527. The median age was 23.8 in 2020, which fits a city with a very large student population.

BYU alone enrolls more than 30,000 students and is the largest private religious university in the country. Academic calendars therefore influence when rentals turn over and when houses sell. If your Provo house has student tenants, plan the closing and any move-out date around the semester.

Provo is the southern end of the FrontRunner commuter rail line, running since December 10, 2012. The Provo Intermodal Center ties together rail, local UTA buses and Greyhound, and Amtrak's California Zephyr stops at the Provo station daily. UVX bus rapid transit, shared with Orem, heads toward Utah Valley University. Provo Municipal Airport is the second-busiest in Utah by aircraft movements, and Allegiant Air has flown from it since 2022. The average commute is 18.4 minutes.

One accessory dwelling unit is permitted on a lot with a one-family detached home, and the owner has to live in the main house or in the unit. Section 14.30.030 of the city code governs this, and it carries real weight for anyone selling a house with a basement or garage apartment.

  • Chapter 6.26 requires a rental dwelling license, renewed yearly.
  • The license lapses one year after approval or at transfer of the property, whichever comes first.
  • A deed restriction describing how the unit is built and occupied is recorded with the Utah County Recorder.
  • Owners prove primary residence with at least two documents, for instance a driver license, vehicle registration, voter card or latest tax return.
  • The unit may house no more than three adults, related or not, plus their minor children.

A buyer must reapply because the license ends on transfer. Courts have upheld owner-occupancy requirements for accessory rentals, in Anderson v. Provo City (2005 UT 5), a case about accessory apartments in single-family zones near BYU. Cities may require a business license for short-term rentals but cannot ban a listing on an online platform.

sections.h2: Selling a house with student tenants
sections.html: Houses near campus often carry leases that run on the school calendar. Tell a buyer which tenants are on a lease, when each term ends and whether the license is current. A buyer who wants to keep renting needs a new license in their own name, so give them the city code section early. If no one is willing to wait for a lease to run out, a cash sale lets the closing be arranged around it instead of forcing an early move-out.

Before the state passed S.B. 284, Provo allowed detached accessory dwellings only in specific overlay zones. The new law reaches parcels of 11,000 square feet or larger with a single-family home, and the city has published a map of projected new eligibility. A proposal under discussion would cap accessory structures at 40 percent of the parcel. If a detached unit is part of your plan or your buyer's, check the current rule with Provo City before you rely on it.

Provo has its own school district, with 13 elementary schools, two middle schools and three high schools. Alpine School District covers a small section of the city. Rain and snow total about 17.2 inches a year near BYU, and temperatures have ranged from a record 108 degrees to minus 30. Buyers' inspectors often ask about the age of the roof, furnace and cooling equipment.

Provo's tax bill is calculated and mailed by Utah County, whose Auditor works from 100 East Center Street, Suite 3600, inside Provo. Valuation notices come at the end of July, and a Board of Equalization appeal on market value is due September 15, which you can file online, by email, by mail or in person. Tax notices follow in mid to late October.

The 45% exemption means a primary residence is taxed on 55% of its market value, provided someone lives there at least 183 consecutive days a year. A rental with a full-time tenant can qualify too, but a vacant or part-time rental is treated as secondary and taxed on full value. Provo has so many rentals that this distinction comes up often. Phone the Treasurer at 801-851-8255 for payoff amounts on delinquent tax.

sections.h2: Selling a Provo house for cash
sections.html:
Typical calls involve a house full of tenants, a rental whose license has lapsed, an inherited property or a place that needs work. Describe the house, and we review it and quote a price based on condition.

The purchase is as-is, so no repairs and no cleaning. Closing goes through a title or escrow company, which files the deed with the Utah County Recorder at 100 East Center Street, Suite 1300. Bring a photo ID to signing, plus estate papers if the house was inherited and a payoff figure if a loan remains. With student tenants, we can time the closing around leases and the academic calendar. No offer obligates you.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Provo house that has an accessory apartment?
faqs.a: Yes. The home must be owner-occupied and carry a rental dwelling license, which ends at transfer, so a buyer has to apply for a fresh one. We purchase the house as it stands.

faqs.q: Does the Provo rental license carry over to a new owner?
faqs.a: No. City code ends the license one year after approval or at transfer, whichever happens first, so a new owner must apply.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to appeal Provo property taxes?
faqs.a: File a valuation appeal with the Utah County Board of Equalization by September 15. A late one is possible through March 31 when it meets extra criteria.

faqs.q: Which county office records a Provo deed?
faqs.a: Deeds are recorded by the Utah County Recorder, 100 East Center Street, Suite 1300. Staff there will not draft documents, advise on law or search titles.

faqs.q: Why is Provo's owner-occupancy rate so low?
faqs.a: Just 39.4% of units are owner-occupied for 2020 to 2024. A big student population around BYU, with a median age of 23.8, means many houses here are rentals.
